product: RECARO Ergomed ES reclining seat with the Climate Package (heated and ventilated, power-adjusted), no side airbag, a left and a right
maker_pn: RECARO Ergomed ES (MPN per trim and side - confirm)
meets: Heat AND cool built in: the RECARO Climate Package (seat heating in cushion and back, plus ventilation through a breathable membrane - fans, not Peltier; the listing does not say, confirm) is part of the ES spec. Power-adjusted: height, cushion tilt, backrest recline (both sides) and the side bolsters of back and cushion, electric; air lumbar; extendable cushion. Controlled by its own switch pack on the seat - an aftermarket seat made to work stand-alone in any car, no CAN, no donor module. Side airbag optional (+GBP 472) - ordered WITHOUT, so nothing pyrotechnic and no lamp. Cushion width 520 mm without bolsters (Recaro measures 120 mm in front of the backrest), height 835 mm max, cushion depth 570 mm max (retailer figures, not Recaro's sheet). GBP 3,835 each without airbag at Tegiwa (2026-10-09, about USD 5,100); a US listing (Evasive Motorsports) showed USD 4,095 for a left seat in the search snippet - that page no longer loads. Used pair with climate seen on eBay.de at EUR 4,999 (ebay.de/itm/297418700975).
why: It is the one seat found that does all three - heat, cooling, power - and is built to be fitted to a car it was not made for: its own switches and its own electronics, so it needs only power and ground, with no CAN, no occupant sensor and no donor module to fool. Recaro is the reference maker for retrofit seats, it can be ordered without the side airbag, and its 520 mm cushion is the narrowest of the climate seats found. Fit to the provision: the seat's climate electronics can take L3-SD / L3-SP pin 1 (heat +, F25/F26 7.5 A) with the DCU's low-side returns as a master enable, so the DCU still turns it on and off; the motors want the reserved motor feed (L3-SDM / L3-SPM).
drawbacks: PRICE: about USD 8,000-10,000 the pair new - far above anything LP52 has budgeted (LP30 + LP31 were USD 80-220 together). Recaro publishes no current: heater, fans and motors are unknown, and the motors need block 01.25 answered (a) - a seat motor on the 25 A comfort output is not possible. Its own switch pack makes the DCU's heat/cool channels an on/off enable only: the dash's seat buttons and the DCU's heat/cool interlock (D-073) become redundant, and if the climate electronics need a constant feed rather than the switched returns the comfort receptacle wiring changes. No Recaro baseframe is listed for a 1979-85 RX-7: the adapter between Recaro's rails and the FB's four seat bolts is custom (fabricated brackets). A power height base raises the hip point in a car with 945 mm (37.2 in) of headroom - a tall driver may sit too high even at the lowest setting. It is a European comfort/orthopaedic seat; its look in an FB is a taste call. 8-10 weeks typical made-to-order lead time (confirm).
confirm: From Recaro or a dealer, before money: the installation sheet - supply voltage, feeds (constant vs ignition), fuse and peak currents of heater, fans and each motor (all unpublished - confirm); whether the climate package is standard or optional on the ES ordered; the switch-pack wiring (can it be enabled by switching its ground, as the DCU's low-side return does). On the car (R11): the floor width between tunnel and sill at the front and rear seat bolts, the four bolt positions and spacing, and the seat's full width over the bolsters (Recaro's 520 mm excludes them) against it; the headroom with the base at its lowest; a US price and lead time.
recommend: Yes only if about USD 8,000-10,000 for the pair is acceptable; if not, say no with the ceiling you want, and the held Lexus IS pair (a few hundred dollars, cooling needing our own controller) goes up next.

product: Audison Prima front set: AP 4 100 mm midbass pair + AP 1 26 mm tweeter pair (with its crossovers)
meets: Maker data, store.elettromedia.com (Elettromedia makes Audison), read 2026-10-09. AP 4 midbass (a pair): 100 mm, 4 ohm, 40 W continuous and 120 W peak, 91 dB SPL, 80 Hz-7.5 kHz, Fs 125 Hz. A passive high-pass at 3.5 kHz, 12 dB/oct, is supplied. It fits the stock 4 in kick-panel location (00-CAR PT662: '4 in dual cone'). why: One family covers every location (Prima AP woofers and tweeters, APX coaxials) with a common voicing. That keeps the fronts, surrounds and centre matched in timbre, as LP58-LP60 require. A separate woofer and tweeter use the separate tweeter runs electrical has already built for this case. The amplifier's DSP can then cross them over actively, and the tweeter at the pillar base raises the stage above a kick-panel coaxial. The 41 mm woofer depth is shallow enough for a kick panel. The three Prima picks (PK039, PK041, PK043) go together, as do the three Hertz Dieci reserves.
drawbacks: A 4 in woofer runs out near 80 Hz, so the sub must carry everything below it: the sub crossover will sit at 80-100 Hz. The kick-panel woofer fires at the driver's shins, so imaging is the DSP's work. The AP 1 tweeter (26 mm) is not the 24 mm tweeter in the APX coaxials: same line and voicing, not the identical driver. Prima is Audison's entry range, below their Voce and Thesis. Safety: if the tweeters are driven actively, the DSP's high-pass (3.5 kHz or higher) must be set before the amplifier is first powered, or the supplied passive filter used. A tweeter fed full-range burns.
confirm: V-103 (the kick-panel opening) against the 93 mm cut-out and 103 mm flange. V-104 (the depth) against 41 mm.
